chapter: Cliff Jackson, Jelly Roll Morton and Harlem in the 1920s
title: Cliff Jackson takes over the Nest Club band from Snowden
summary: Snowden moved to the Bandville Club and gave his Nest Club job to Cliff Jackson, whose band Caldwell joined and named A Bunch of Keys.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, so then, according to this, now, after Bobby Brown worked with Snowden.
I worked with Snowden. That's right.
Snowden had a group. It was Prince Robinson (unintelligible) because they had a very good band -- at the Nest Club. So they had a club on 129th Street, just off of

Bom (unintelligible) called the Bandville Club, the Bom Bandville Club. So he had the job at the Bandville, so he took his band out of the Nest Club and gave it to his -- gave the group to Cliff Jackson, let -- Jackson formed the group to play in the Nest Club. So Cliff picked his group, and I was with Cliff. Cliff had almost as good a band as Snowden did. He and Snowden were both from Washington, D. C. Well, Snowden was very impressed with the group, so Cliff said -- he asked Cliff, said, what are you going to name the band? Cliff said, let me think. It's a (unintelligible) band. Say, Cliff, you're the band leader, what are you going to name it? A bunch of keys, because we were playing all the keys, see?
